accepted.sentence: Growers commonly start new plants from crowns, slips, or basal shoots, preserving cultivated traits without relying on seed.
Ethylene-releasing treatments can trigger flowering more uniformly, helping growers coordinate fruit development and harvest timing.
This drought-adapted plant takes in much of its carbon dioxide at night, storing it for photosynthesis during daylight.
At harvest, workers cut mature fruit from its stalk by hand or with tools, then sort it for shipment.
For canning, prepared pieces are heated and sealed in containers, often packed with juice or a sweetened liquid.
Shipments are kept cool but not excessively cold, since chilling can damage the flesh and outer tissues.
It gains little sweetness after picking, so harvest maturity strongly influences the fruit’s eventual eating quality.
Cross-pollination can lead to seed formation in developing fruit, so commercial growers may limit access by pollinating animals.
